note: Owner-approved card text for the What can I build catalogue. Show exactly as written, in Debug and Release.

cards.name: The Garden
cards.what: A garden with fruit trees and a river, plus separate story pieces: Noah's ark, the tower of Babel, and the tents and wells of Abraham's family.
cards.why: Genesis begins with God planting a garden in Eden for the first people (Genesis 2:8–10), then follows the flood, Babel and Abraham's family (Genesis 6–50).

cards.name: Mount Sinai
cards.what: The mountain where Israel camped, with a burning bush, a path through the parted sea, and tents at its foot.
cards.why: God spoke to Moses from a burning bush, led Israel through the sea, and gave the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai (Exodus 3, 14, 19–20).

cards.name: The Tabernacle Courts
cards.what: A linen courtyard with the bronze altar and basin. Inside are the lampstand, the bread table and the incense altar, with the ark behind the veil.
cards.why: God told Israel to make a sanctuary so he could live among them (Exodus 25:8). Leviticus gives his instructions for worship there (Leviticus 1, 16).

cards.name: The Wilderness Camp
cards.what: Tribal tents set out under their banners, a bronze snake on a pole, and water flowing from a rock.
cards.why: Israel camped by tribes in the wilderness (Numbers 2). God gave water from the rock (Numbers 20) and healed those who looked at the bronze snake (Numbers 21:8–9).

cards.name: Mount Nebo Lookout
cards.what: A stone path up a hill to a lookout over the Promised Land.
cards.why: Moses taught Israel God's law before they entered the land. Then he climbed Mount Nebo, where God showed him the whole land (Deuteronomy 34:1–4).

cards.name: Jericho Gate
cards.what: Memorial stones from the Jordan, a camp at Gilgal, Jericho's fallen walls, and fields marked out for each tribe.
cards.why: Israel crossed the Jordan and set up stones to remember it (Joshua 4). Jericho's walls fell (Joshua 6), and the land was shared among the tribes (Joshua 13–21).

cards.name: The Judges' Hilltop
cards.what: Deborah's palm tree, a winepress, a fleece on a threshing floor, and watchtowers.
cards.why: Deborah judged Israel under a palm tree (Judges 4:5). Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress when God called him, then asked for a sign with a fleece (Judges 6).

cards.name: The Farmstead
cards.what: A farmhouse, barley and wheat fields, a threshing floor and the town gate.
cards.why: Ruth gathered grain in Boaz's fields at harvest. She met him at the threshing floor, and he redeemed her at Bethlehem's town gate (Ruth 2–4).

cards.name: Shiloh and the Valley
cards.what: The house of the Lord at Shiloh, a shepherd's field, and the Valley of Elah with its stream and stones.
cards.why: Samuel grew up serving at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1–3). David the shepherd chose five smooth stones from a stream to face Goliath (1 Samuel 17:40).

cards.name: The City of David
cards.what: A walled hill city with David's house, the tent for the ark, terraces and towers.
cards.why: David took Jerusalem, built his house there, and brought the ark into the tent he had set up for it (2 Samuel 5:7–11; 6:17).

cards.name: Solomon's Temple
cards.what: The temple with cedar beams and two bronze pillars, Solomon's palace, and Elijah's altar on a hillside.
cards.why: Solomon built the temple and his palace in Jerusalem (1 Kings 6–7). Later, God answered Elijah with fire on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18).

cards.name: The Kings' Road
cards.what: Elisha's rooftop room, the Jordan River, chariots and city walls along a road. These are different places from different stories.
cards.why: A woman of Shunem made a room for Elisha (2 Kings 4:8–11), and Naaman was healed in the Jordan (2 Kings 5:14). The book follows the kings of Israel and Judah.

cards.name: The Record House
cards.what: A symbolic house of scroll shelves and family-line banners, with musicians and supplies for the temple.
cards.why: 1 Chronicles opens with Israel's family records (chapters 1–9). Then David appoints musicians and gathers what's needed for the temple (chapters 15–16, 29).

cards.name: The Temple Courtyard
cards.what: Temple courts, a great bronze basin, a gathering square and repair scaffolding.
cards.why: Solomon made a huge bronze basin for the temple (2 Chronicles 4:2). Later kings like Joash and Josiah repaired the temple (2 Chronicles 24, 34).

cards.name: The Rebuilt Altar
cards.what: Rubble cleared away and the altar rebuilt, then the foundation and walls of the second temple.
cards.why: Exiles came home from Babylon, rebuilt the altar, laid the temple's foundation and finished the house of God (Ezra 3; 6:15).

cards.name: The City Wall
cards.what: Wall sections and gates rising with workers' scaffolds, and a wooden platform for reading.
cards.why: Nehemiah led the people to rebuild Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3–6). Ezra then read the Law to them from a wooden platform (Nehemiah 8:4).

cards.name: The Persian Palace
cards.what: A palace gate, a royal garden and a banquet hall.
cards.why: Esther became queen in the Persian king's palace. She risked her life at a banquet to save her people, and they still remember it at Purim (Esther 2, 7, 9).

cards.name: The Ash Heap Farm
cards.what: An ash heap that becomes a farm, with herds and a household restored.
cards.why: Job sat in ashes in his suffering (Job 2:8). At the end, God restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as before (Job 42:10–12).

cards.name: The Music Garden
cards.what: Harps, terraces, fountains and flowers, growing piece by piece.
cards.why: Psalms is Israel's songbook of praise and prayer, sung with harps and lyres (Psalm 33:2; 150).

cards.name: The House of Wisdom
cards.what: A house with seven pillars, seats by the gate, an ant hill and a fruitful vine.
cards.why: Wisdom is pictured building her house with seven pillars (Proverbs 9:1) and calling out at the city gates (Proverbs 8:3). The ant shows how to work hard (Proverbs 6:6).

cards.name: The Sundial Garden
cards.what: A garden that changes with the seasons, with a sundial, a wind vane and a quiet bench as symbols of time.
cards.why: Ecclesiastes says there is a time for everything (3:1–8) and watches the sun and the wind go round and round (1:5–6).

cards.name: The Vineyard Garden
cards.what: Vines, lilies and pomegranates inside a garden wall with a fountain.
cards.why: The Song pictures love as a locked garden with a fountain, full of pomegranates, among vineyards and lilies (Song of Songs 2:1; 4:12–15).

cards.name: The Prophet's Mountain
cards.what: A path up a mountain, a stump with a new shoot, a highway in the desert, and a meadow where the wolf lives with the lamb.
cards.why: Isaiah sees nations coming to God's mountain (2:2–3), a shoot from Jesse's stump (11:1), peace between animals (11:6–7) and a highway of holiness (35:8).

cards.name: The Potter's House
cards.what: A potter's wheel, clay jars, an almond branch and a muddy cistern.
cards.why: God showed Jeremiah an almond branch (1:11–12) and sent him to watch a potter shape clay (18). Jeremiah was later lowered into a muddy cistern (38:6).

cards.name: The Mourning Wall
cards.what: Broken stones and small memorial lights.
cards.why: Lamentations grieves Jerusalem after its fall, yet holds on to hope because God's mercies are new every morning (3:22–23).

cards.name: The Valley and the River
cards.what: A valley of dry bones coming to life, a temple, and a river lined with trees.
cards.why: Ezekiel saw dry bones become a living army, a picture of Israel restored (37:1–14). He also saw a river flowing from the temple with fruit trees on its banks (47:1–12).

cards.name: The Exile Court
cards.what: A royal court, a great statue, a furnace, a lions' den and a window open for prayer.
cards.why: These come from different stories in Daniel: the king's dream of a statue (2), the fiery furnace (3), and Daniel praying at his window before the lions' den (6).

cards.name: The Restored Farm
cards.what: A dry field that turns into a vineyard and grain.
cards.why: Hosea promises that when Israel returns to God, they will grow like grain and blossom like a vine (Hosea 14:7).

cards.name: The Harvest Fields
cards.what: Fields stripped by locusts that grow back full.
cards.why: Locusts destroyed Judah's crops (1:4), and God promised to restore the years the locusts had eaten (2:25).

cards.name: The Shepherd's Orchard
cards.what: A sheepfold, sycamore-fig trees, a plumb line and a basket of fruit.
cards.why: Amos was a shepherd who looked after sycamore figs (7:14). God showed him a plumb line (7:7–8) and a basket of summer fruit (8:1–2).

cards.name: The Cliff Fortress
cards.what: A fortress high in the cliffs, finished in one read.
cards.why: Obadiah warns Edom, who lived in the clefts of the rock, that their pride would bring them down (1:3–4).

cards.name: The Harbour
cards.what: A dock at Joppa, a ship, a great fish and a shade plant.
cards.why: Jonah ran from God on a ship from Joppa, was swallowed by a great fish, and later sat under a plant God provided (1:3, 1:17, 4:6).

cards.name: Little Bethlehem
cards.what: A small town of houses with a vine and a fig tree.
cards.why: Micah foretold a ruler coming from little Bethlehem (5:2) and a day when everyone sits under their own vine and fig tree (4:4).

cards.name: The River Gate
cards.what: Nineveh's river gates and a river channel.
cards.why: Nahum foretold Nineveh's fall, when its river gates are opened and the palace melts away (2:6). The gates mark the city's judgment.

cards.name: The Watchtower
cards.what: A watchtower, a tablet stand, and a deer on the heights.
cards.why: Habakkuk waited at his watchpost for God's answer and was told to write the vision on tablets (2:1–2). He trusted God to make his feet like a deer's (3:19).

cards.name: The Singing Square
cards.what: A town square that fills with people and song.
cards.why: Zephaniah ends with God gathering his people and rejoicing over them with singing (3:14–20).

cards.name: The Temple Builders' Yard
cards.what: Stacks of stone and a temple wall rising.
cards.why: Haggai urged the people back from exile to stop neglecting God's house and rebuild the temple (1:4–8, 14).

cards.name: The Lampstand Court
cards.what: A gold lampstand between two olive trees, horses, and a city without walls.
cards.why: These come from separate visions: horses among myrtle trees (1:8), Jerusalem without walls (2:4–5) and the lampstand with two olive trees (4:2–3).

cards.name: The Storehouse
cards.what: A storehouse that fills up, a refiner's fire and a sunrise.
cards.why: God invites his people to bring the full tithe into the storehouse (3:10), promises to refine them like silver (3:2–3), and speaks of the sun of righteousness rising (4:2).

cards.name: Fishing Village
cards.what: A fishing hut, boats, a hillside, homes and a market by the lake.
cards.why: Jesus made his home in Capernaum (4:13), called fishermen by the Sea of Galilee (4:18–22), and taught the Sermon on the Mount on a hillside (5–7).

cards.name: Lakeside Village
cards.what: A hut, a boat on the water, nets and a meadow for crowds.
cards.why: Jesus called fishermen from their nets (1:16–20), taught the crowd from a boat (4:1), and fed 5,000 people sitting on green grass (6:39–44).

cards.name: Shepherds' Village
cards.what: A manger, a shepherds' field, homes and a road with an inn.
cards.why: Jesus was laid in a manger, and shepherds came from the fields to see him (2:7–16). The roadside inn comes from the Good Samaritan story (10:30–35).

cards.name: Vineyard Village
cards.what: A wedding at Cana, Jacob's well, a vineyard and a garden tomb. These are separate places.
cards.why: Jesus turned water into wine at Cana (2), met a woman at Jacob's well (4:5–6), called himself the true vine (15:1–5), and was buried in a garden tomb (19:41–42).

cards.name: The Upper Room Town
cards.what: An upper room that grows into a town, with a road and a harbour where a ship is wrecked.
cards.why: The disciples gathered in an upper room (1:13), the church grew in Jerusalem (2), and the gospel travelled by road and sea, including Paul's shipwreck (27).

cards.name: Rome Road Town
cards.what: A small town on the coast road, a letter post and an olive tree.
cards.why: Paul wrote this letter to the believers in Rome (1:7). He pictured God's people as an olive tree with new branches grafted in (11:17–24).

cards.name: Corinth Workshop
cards.what: A tentmaker's shop, a gathering house and a market.
cards.why: In Corinth, Paul made tents with Aquila and Priscilla (Acts 18:1–3). His letter speaks about the church gathering together and food sold in the market (10:25; 11).

cards.name: Corinth Harbour
cards.what: A port with jars of clay holding treasure.
cards.why: Paul says we hold the treasure of the gospel in jars of clay, to show the power belongs to God (4:7).

cards.name: Galatian Fruit Garden
cards.what: A garden with nine kinds of fruit.
cards.why: Paul names nine fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control (5:22–23).

cards.name: Ephesus Armoury
cards.what: A home with pieces of armour on stands.
cards.why: Paul tells believers to put on the full armour of God: belt, breastplate, shoes, shield, helmet and sword (6:10–18).

cards.name: Philippi Riverside
cards.what: A riverside prayer spot, Lydia's house and a prison.
cards.why: On his first visit to Philippi, Paul met Lydia by the river and was jailed with Silas (Acts 16:13–40). Philippians is his letter back to that church.

cards.name: Colossae Hilltown
cards.what: Hillside houses and a deeply rooted tree.
cards.why: Paul urges believers to be rooted and built up in Christ (2:6–7).

cards.name: Thessalonica Lamp Street
cards.what: A street of homes with lamps lit.
cards.why: Paul calls believers children of light who stay awake and ready for Jesus' return (5:4–8).

cards.name: Thessalonica Workshop
cards.what: Work benches and tools.
cards.why: Paul reminds the church he worked night and day so he wouldn't be a burden, and tells them to work quietly too (3:7–12).

cards.name: The Teacher's House
cards.what: A house church with a scroll table.
cards.why: Paul writes about how to live in God's household, the church (3:15), and tells Timothy to give himself to reading Scripture and teaching (4:13).

cards.name: The Scroll Room
cards.what: A cloak on a peg, with books and parchments.
cards.why: In his last letter, Paul asks Timothy to bring his cloak, books and parchments (4:13), and reminds him that all Scripture is God-breathed (3:16).

cards.name: Crete Village
cards.what: An island village with a harbour.
cards.why: Paul left Titus on the island of Crete to put things in order and appoint elders in every town (1:5).

cards.name: The Welcome House
cards.what: A house with an open door, finished in one read.
cards.why: Paul asks Philemon to welcome back Onesimus as a brother, the way he would welcome Paul himself (1:15–17).

cards.name: The Hall of Faith
cards.what: A hall that fills with banners, and an anchor.
cards.why: Hebrews 11 remembers people who lived by faith, and the letter calls our hope an anchor for the soul (6:19).

cards.name: The Well and Garden
cards.what: A well, a garden and a small ship's rudder.
cards.why: James compares the tongue to a small rudder that steers a ship (3:4–5) and a spring that can't give both fresh and salt water (3:11–12).

cards.name: Living Stones House
cards.what: A house built stone by stone.
cards.why: Peter says believers are like living stones being built into a spiritual house (2:4–5).

cards.name: The Lamp Path
cards.what: A lamp lighting a dark path.
cards.why: Peter calls God's prophetic word a lamp shining in a dark place (1:19).

cards.name: The Light House
cards.what: A house that brightens chapter by chapter.
cards.why: John writes that God is light, and those who walk in the light share life with him and each other (1:5–7).

cards.name: The Lady's Cottage
cards.what: A small symbolic cottage, finished in one read.
cards.why: John writes to "the chosen lady and her children", which may mean a woman or a church, urging them to walk in truth and love (1:1–6).

cards.name: The Guest House
cards.what: A symbolic place of welcome for travellers, finished in one read.
cards.why: John praises Gaius for welcoming and supporting travelling believers (1:5–8).

cards.name: The Keeper's Tower
cards.what: A small symbolic tower, finished in one read.
cards.why: Jude urges believers to keep themselves in God's love, and praises God, who is able to keep them from stumbling (1:20–24).

cards.name: The New Jerusalem
cards.what: Patmos, seven lampstands, and the New Jerusalem with pearl gates, the river of life and the tree of life.
cards.why: John received his visions on Patmos and saw Jesus among seven lampstands, the churches (1:9–20). He saw the holy city lit by God's glory, with the river and tree of life (21–22).
